admission.justification: Future link-target work must distinguish content edits from the implemented removed-path/route/symbol obligations, and reader work cannot infer content currentness from serialization or locator resolution.

alternatives.option: Raise no removed-target item for a content-only edit at a still-existing retrieval target; do not promise reader stale-body observation.
alternatives.reason: A non-reconsideration record link is a retrieval pointer: a content-only edit at a still-existing target raises no link_target obligation. Removal of a previously present path, route or symbol has its existing literal-target repair domain. The inspected reader serializes stored anchors without a stale-body comparison; R73 attribution in the historical appendix does not prove that display is delivered.

alternatives.option: Raise a worklist obligation merely because that retrieval pointer body changed.

alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if the owning approved requirement is explicitly revised to authorize this changed boundary; this prose is not a computed trigger.

consequences: No content-only link_target obligation is introduced; removed-target obligations remain.
A body-stale reader label is not certified by this decision or by the historical R73 attribution.
context: MIK-R55 appendix entry 50 retains the no-content-only-link_target-obligation boundary. Its historical assertion that the reader shows changed link bodies as stale is not an implemented guarantee of the inspected knowledge_reader truth/decision path; only stored anchor rendering and locator resolution are established.
